newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks at '96 high despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks at '96 high despite profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended only a fraction higher on Friday but managed a new 1996 closing high despite late profit-taking that erased earlier gains.

The weighted index hit a 1996 intra-session peak of 6,642.73 points at the open but ended only 4.63 points or 0.07 percent higher at 6,616.21, which nonetheless was a new closing high for the year. Turnover was an active T$51.39 billion.
Prices opened on momentum from Thursday's rise, which broke psychological resistance and gave the index more upside room.
"The profit-taking that happened later was expected," said Wang Jieh of Foremost Investment.
"Although market sentiment is generally sound, it is not bullish enough to keep on setting new highs without profit-taking," Wang added.

Gains were concentrated in the electronics sector, which rose 1.10 percent on expectations of sound profit reports as an October 31 deadline approaches for firms to release profit and sales results for the first three quarters.

First International Computer gained T$1 to end at T$39.30 with the session's single heaviest trade volume, reflecting news that it was negotiating an order with U.S. giant Compaq Computer Corp to make Compaq motherboards.
Shares in the financial and textile sectors suffered from profit-taking against their recent gains, slipping 0.54 percent and 0.32 percent respectively.
"Various sectors will take turns performing in the next several weeks, but electronics probably will outdo the market as profit reports come in," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming.
Brokers expected the index to consolidate before seeking new highs. A 6,590-6,640 range was seen for Saturday.
